h1: River Residence Saraburi — A Budget Hotel With Balcony Rooms and Easy Parking in Saraburi City
intro: If you want a cheap place to overnight in Saraburi city that isn't on a busy road and has easy parking, River Residence Saraburi is a small hotel in Takut, a few kilometres from the centre. What guests like best is that many rooms have balconies, the setting is quiet, and the free parking is generous · Rooms are simple, with AC, TV and free Wi-Fi — comfortable enough for a night at a budget price. To be straight about it, the draw here is the quiet, the parking and the price, not luxury or full facilities, and there is no breakfast · It suits drivers passing through or people in town on errands who want a quiet room and easy parking, rather than anyone after a full-service resort · From approx. ฿700/night.

body.html: What guests mention most about River Residence Saraburi is the quiet setting, the balconies on many rooms, and the generous free parking · The hotel sits in Takut, Mueang Saraburi, about 3 km from the city centre, in an area that isn't busy, so it's quieter than hotels on the main road · Several reviews describe it as a handy overnight stop for drivers passing through Saraburi or visiting town on business, because parking is easy and you get a quiet room at a low price.

The hotel itself offers simple, no-frills rooms · Options range from a single-bed Standard up to double rooms, all with AC, TV, a private bathroom and free Wi-Fi · A point guests like is that many rooms have a balcony or terrace to sit out on, and some say the rooms feel more spacious than expected for the price · The building has an elevator, a 24-hour front desk and a cafe · But it's worth flagging up front that there is no breakfast and no pool — this is a stopover hotel that's about quiet and price rather than facilities.
"Loads of parking, clean room, a balcony you can sit on, and a quiet, peaceful feel — a good-value place for an overnight stop."

The location is the quiet-but-still-close kind: away from the busy streets, yet only a short drive into central Saraburi · It's roughly 5–10 minutes by car to the town centre, Saraburi train station and the city's restaurants · It's within easy driving distance of Saraburi's nature spots such as Muak Lek and the national-park waterfalls · From Bangkok it's about 90 minutes' drive, making it a sensible stopover or base for a road trip that uses Saraburi as a waypoint.

The honest weak spots are soundproofing between rooms and inconsistent bathroom upkeep · Some real reviews note that the walls don't block sound well, so you can hear neighbouring rooms, and there are reports of worn or damaged bathroom fittings in certain rooms · This is a budget hotel with a fairly small number of reviews on some platforms, so scores can swing · If you expect a sleek new property or a resort with full facilities, this isn't it — but if you can accept simple rooms in exchange for a low price, quiet and easy parking, it's still a usable choice.

On price · standard rooms on booking platforms start around ฿590–฿900/night depending on season and room type · Review scores across platforms vary quite a bit, from roughly 5.8 to 7.5 off a handful to a few dozen reviews, which reflects how much your experience depends on the specific room you get · The praise lands on parking, quiet, balconies and value; the soft spots are soundproofing and uneven upkeep.

Bottom line from real guest sentiment: River Residence Saraburi suits drivers passing through or people in town on errands who want a quiet room, easy parking and a low price more than anyone after a full-service resort with a pool and breakfast · Set your expectations to match what it is — a simple, quiet budget hotel with balcony rooms and roomy parking — and you can overnight comfortably in Saraburi city without spending much.

honestChecks: If you expect a resort with a pool and breakfast — this is a simple stopover hotel with no pool and no breakfast → choose a resort in the Muak Lek or Kaeng Khoi area instead.
If you just want a quiet, cheap, easy-to-park room in Saraburi city — the quiet, balconies and parking deliver → a great fit for a road trip or an overnight errand stop.
If you're a light sleeper — some reviews note the walls don't block sound well → ask for a room not adjoining another, or a floor with fewer guests, to sleep better.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — River Residence Saraburi

faq.q: Where is River Residence Saraburi · what's nearby?
faq.a: The hotel is in Takut, Mueang Saraburi District, about 3 km from the city centre · It's roughly 5–10 minutes by car to central Saraburi, the train station and restaurants · It sits in a quiet area off the busy roads · From Bangkok it's about a 90-minute drive.

faq.q: How much does River Residence Saraburi cost · what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at approx. ฿700/night · Options range from Standard and Standard Double to Superior and a Family / Twin room around ฿950 · Many rooms have a balcony · Prices vary by season and room type — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does River Residence Saraburi have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: It has generous free parking, which guests often praise, but no breakfast (there is a cafe on site) and no pool · If you want a resort with a pool and breakfast, look at the Muak Lek or Kaeng Khoi area instead.

faq.q: Who is River Residence Saraburi best for?
faq.a: It's best for drivers passing through Saraburi or people in town on errands who want a quiet room, easy parking and a low price · It's about quiet, balconies and parking rather than being a full-service resort with a pool.

faq.q: What are the rooms and service like at River Residence Saraburi?
faq.a: Straight from real reviews · the praise lands on roomy parking, quiet, balcony rooms and value · The trade-offs are weak soundproofing, so you can hear next door, and some worn bathroom fittings in certain rooms · There aren't many reviews yet, so scores can swing.

faq.q: What's the easiest way to get to River Residence Saraburi?
faq.a: Driving yourself is easiest, since the hotel has generous free parking and sits off the busy roads · From Bangkok, take Phahonyothin Road toward Saraburi, about 90 minutes · Having a car also makes it easy to reach central Saraburi and continue on to Muak Lek or the waterfalls.
